claims.statement: Poisson 1837 Bachelier book titled Recherches sur la probabilité des jugements
Stigler 1982 translated relevant passages and found Poisson's eponymous law around original p206 rather than central to book
Poisson's 1837 argument concerned cumulative near-rare-event approximations, not modern independent mass formula notation
De Moivre's earlier eighteenth-century work foreshadowed rare-event approximations; originality attribution is not exclusive
Modern binomial-to-Poisson law for n large p=λ/n fixed λ gives P(X=k)→e^-λ λ^k/k!
Modern Poisson(2) gives P0=e^-2 P1=2e^-2 P2=2e^-2 and P3=4e^-2/3
Poisson distribution normalizes to one and has expectation and variance λ
Mixture of independent Poisson rates 1 and 3 with 50/50 environments has mean 2 variance 3 and P0=(e^-1+e^-3)/2
Independent Poisson variables with means λ1 and λ2 sum to Poisson(λ1+λ2)
The short rare-count approximation needs a specified limiting regime; dependence and variable rates can break naive applications
Bortkiewicz's 1898 law of small numbers was later expansion and not Poisson's 1837 original demonstration
Historical applications across space time need empirical scrutiny and not every low count is Poisson
